I'm also comfortable on the frontend with Angular, which is what this page is built with. I like self-study, understanding what happens underneath the tools I use, and teaching when someone needs a hand.

PROJECTS.DUCKY.SUMMARY: Moderation bot for a Twitch channel: three subsystems in one Python process, with a Rust desktop agent and semantic memory on pgvector.
PROJECTS.DUCKY.DESCRIPTION: A moderation bot for chaarqueen's Twitch channel, built as three subsystems running inside a single Python process, each starting independently depending on the configuration available. The auto-categorizer detects which game is running and updates the stream category, using two sources: a desktop agent written in Rust (an 800 KB executable with no runtime dependencies) that watches the machine's processes, and Discord presence as a fallback; if the agent stops reporting for 210 seconds, the bot falls back to Discord on its own. The chat bot connects over Twitch IRC and answers commands with live LoL and Valorant stats from the Riot API. The clips pipeline pulls the day's clips with yt-dlp and uploads them to Google Drive. The most interesting part is the chat memory: every message is stored in PostgreSQL and queued so a background worker generates embeddings in batches of 100 against Gemini, stores them with pgvector, and then enables semantic search by cosine similarity to summarise or search the conversation. It ships with an Angular dashboard, is dockerized, and has CI on GitHub Actions with SonarQube analysis.
PROJECTS.THEATER.SUMMARY: Theater ticket booking REST API built with Spring Boot 3 and PostgreSQL, dockerized and deployed on AWS.
PROJECTS.THEATER.DESCRIPTION: A theater booking system built with Spring Boot 3 and PostgreSQL, fully dockerized with Docker Compose. It exposes a RESTful API documented with Swagger UI (OpenAPI) to manage events, tickets and bookings, with a data model covering different event types (play, concert, talk), ticket stock, discounts and customer attendance. The infrastructure runs on AWS: the API on an EC2 instance behind Nginx as an HTTPS reverse proxy, and the database on Amazon RDS inside a private subnet, reachable only from the application's security group. Deployment is automated with GitHub Actions.
PROJECTS.CS2D.SUMMARY: Round-based 2D multiplayer game inspired by Counter-Strike 1.6, built in C++ with SDL2 and a client-server architecture.
PROJECTS.CS2D.DESCRIPTION: Final project for Taller de Programación I (FIUBA), developed by a team of three. It's a round-based 2D multiplayer game inspired by the classic Counter-Strike 1.6, with a client-server architecture over TCP sockets and a multithreaded model: the server owns the match state and clients consume it in real time. The client is written in C++ with SDL2 (graphics, audio and fonts) and the map editor in Qt6. It includes a lobby for creating and finding matches, team and skin selection, weapon buying, rounds, and health and money systems. The project builds with CMake, runs on Linux, is dockerized, and has CI on GitHub Actions running builds, tests and pre-commit hooks.
PROJECTS.REDES.SUMMARY: Interactive study guide for the Networks course (FIUBA): the TCP/IP stack layer by layer, with search and a quiz mode.
PROJECTS.REDES.DESCRIPTION: An Angular app that walks through the TCP/IP stack layer by layer following Kurose & Ross: fundamentals, application, transport, network (data and control planes), link, wireless and security. Each section explains the concepts at the depth the final exam requires, flagging the usual traps and frequently asked questions. It includes a global search, a revision cheat sheet, and a quiz mode with 66 oral-exam-style questions, filterable by section and with an explanation for every answer. Deployed on Vercel.
PROJECTS.CONCURRENTES.SUMMARY: Interactive study guide for Concurrent Programming (FIUBA), with simulations of locks, Petri nets and distributed systems.
PROJECTS.CONCURRENTES.DESCRIPTION: An Angular app covering FIUBA's Concurrent Programming Techniques course, from threads and locks to distributed systems, with Rust as the reference language. What sets it apart from a plain summary are the interactive simulations: data races, semaphores, dining philosophers, actors, leader election and two-phase commit. It also includes a Petri net simulator where you can fire transitions and watch the marking evolve live, with the classic models preloaded (mutex, bounded producer-consumer, client-server, reader-writer, inhibitor arc, barber and banker). Deployed on Vercel.
PROJECTS.SA_MICRO.SUMMARY: Two Java microservices with a BFF composing data across both, documented with OpenAPI and secured with Basic Auth.
PROJECTS.SA_MICRO.DESCRIPTION: Final project for the microservices module of the Sistemas Activos S.R.L training. Two Java and Spring Boot microservices, each with its own database schema, plus a BFF (Backend For Frontend) built with Spring WebFlux and WebClient that composes data from both into a single response. Everything behind a RESTful API documented with Swagger (OpenAPI 3), with pagination, Basic Auth on every service including the BFF, and the data layer handled through JPA and Hibernate. It also includes an Actuator project with its own schema for metrics, a Thymeleaf interface exercising all four HTTP verbs, and a Postman collection to test the flow. Managed with Maven and dockerized.
PROJECTS.TP_BDD.SUMMARY: Python script that computes statistics over PostgreSQL and caches the results in Redis.
PROJECTS.TP_BDD.DESCRIPTION: A Databases course project. The script connects to a PostgreSQL database holding people and countries, computes statistics (overall and per-country average age, gender distribution, most frequent gender per country, youngest and oldest person, and the top 3 countries by population) and stores every result in Redis so later queries are instant. Credentials are handled through environment variables and the project ships with the SQL schema creation script.
PROJECTS.INVENTORY.SUMMARY: Python inventory management system, with support for six languages and CI on GitHub Actions.
PROJECTS.INVENTORY.DESCRIPTION: An inventory management system written in Python. It supports adding, updating, removing, listing and searching items, as well as listing everything below a given stock threshold. It's localized into six languages (English, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, Russian and German) and has continuous integration on GitHub Actions running the test suite on every push.
PROJECTS.INFINITY_MATH.SUMMARY: A very basic private-lessons website built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
PROJECTS.INFINITY_MATH.DESCRIPTION: Infinity Math is a very basic private-lessons website built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The site has a home page, the lessons, the location and a contact form. It is responsive and looks good on mobile devices, and although it doesn't have real information, it's a good example of what a private-lessons website would look like. Deployed on Netlify.
